 Media Erin Andrews set for 300th NFL game, with eye on more morning show work, growing Wear fashion line
 By Austin Karp 11.06.2026 Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Share current article via %{socialType} Erin Andrews will celebrate her 300th NFL game on Sunday. FOX SPORTS Fox Sports will have its “A” team at Packers-Patriots on Sunday afternoon, and beyond it being Tom Brady’s return to Foxborough, it brings another big talent milestone -- Erin Andrews’ 300th NFL game.
 Andrews, who is represented by SMAC Entertainment, first came over to Fox in 2012 and has re-signed three times with the network, most recently before the 2025 season. She gave credit to Brad Zager, Fox Sports’ president and executive producer, for creating a culture that has kept her and others around.
 “We just all genuinely enjoy being together,” Andrews said of her team at Fox, which includes Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady and Tom Rinaldi on the talent side. “Brad put us all together and he put the pieces with this puzzle together and knew it was going to work and has allowed us to grow and create this family. And I’m so grateful for the opportunity to be a part of it and that he put me in this place.”
 Andrews has continued to branch out beyond work on the sports broadcasting side. That started years ago when she was a co-host for ABC’s “Dancing With The Stars,” and currently, she’s co-host of the “99 to Beat” game show alongside actor Ken Jeong.
 Last year, she filled in for a week as co-host of the “Jenna & Friends” segment on NBC’s “Today” show. Andrews tells SBJ she’d “love” to do more of that. “I want to do it again. I would love to work for a morning show,” Andrews said. “Michael Strahan seems to have that down, and yeah, it’d be something I’d be interested in looking into doing in the future.”
 Andrews also co-hosts the podcast “Calm Down” alongside Charissa Thompson, which is produced by The Volume and iHeartMedia and just dropped its 429th episode this week. 
 “Every Monday morning, Charissa and I either talk on the phone or we leave each other really long voice notes about how the weekend went, what it was like traveling. … How the game went. What’s going on with other games. And we just decided ‘let’s put this in a podcast,’” she said. “We just started talking about what life was like in our industry as best friends, as females, traveling on the road. We have a segment that we do called ‘Travels and Tribulations’ where we just talk about kind of almost like Larry David-esque ‘Seinfeld’ situations, because traveling is wild.”
 Beyond TV and podcasts, Andrews continues to grow her fashion line, “Wear by Erin Andrews,” which she co-founded with SMAC CEO Constance Schwartz-Morini. That line, which Schwartz-Morini discusses on this week’s SBJ Sports Media Podcast , started with the 32 NFL teams, but has expanded to include the NHL, WNBA, MLB, NBA, NCAA, NWSL, WWE and other leagues.
 “Besides my real-life baby at home, this is my baby, and I’m super proud of it,” she said. “We’ve had a lot of doors closed in our face. We had a lot of people say, ‘It’s a good idea, but maybe not.’ We had this idea, we stuck with it. We kept knocking on doors and grateful that Fanatics gave us a shot . … We just got into Costco, which is super great. It’s just really exciting all the things that we’re doing and seeing every Sunday when I’m flying home, all the women that are wearing our apparel to the games or just around the house.”
 Also celebrating his 300th NFL broadcast is NBC Sports’ Mike Tirico , who will be on the call for Buccaneers-Bears on “Sunday Night Football.” Colleagues praised Tirico’s prep and dedication in a piece at The Athletic .
